newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bills seen in low demand, zloty eyes Ruch.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bills seen in low demand, zloty eyes Ruch.

text.p: Low yields of T-bills compared to yields of the central bank paper and the possible official rate rise are likely to keep domestic banks and foreign investors on the sidelines at Monday's primary T-bill tender, dealers said.
They said demand at the auction was likely to total half of the one billion zloty offer with the majority of bids placed for the benchmark 52-week paper. @
"Demand at the auction is likely to be small, beause banks prefer to invest in the much higher yielding National Bank of Poland's bills," said Andrzej Hirsz, senior T-bill dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
The average accepted yield of the 182-day NBP-bill at Friday's tender was 21.99 while the average yield of the 26-week T-bill at the lat primary auction was 19.30 percent.
Likewise, the average yield of the 91-day NBP-bill was 21.96 percent on Friday against an average yield of 18.81 percent of 13-week T-bills. @

"Foreign investors are unlikely to save the Monday auction because they are unlikely to buy zloty instruments before the expected central bank rate rise," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.

The NBP has repeatedly warned Poles that it might be forced to rise its official interest rates early this year if the fast growth of credit for households does not slow down. Credit for households is estimated to have doubled last year.
Dealers said T-bills at the primary auction were likely to be sought mostly by large non-banking clients, who cannot buy NBP-bills or banks buying the paper on client orders. @

Dealers said the large gap between yields of T-bills and NBP-bills also froze trade on the secndary T-bill market as traders did not want to buy such low-yielding instrument and were reluctant to sell it at higher yields and carry a loss.
"There is nothing going on on the secondary market now," one dealer said.

Dealers said the zloty was likely to ride anchor at around three percent from the trading band centre next week, waiting for the pending privatisation of the Ruch news-stand chain to push it upwards. @

Newspapers have reported that the French Hachette Distribution Services firm agreed to pay $55 million for a majority stake in Ruch and the treasury ministry said a decision on the sale could be taken next week.
The zloty ended the week at stronger 3.10/3.06 percent from the trading band centre at 2.8685/15 against the dollar and 1.8475/95 against the mark.
